To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the decomposition of the oscillator fluctuations is not unique, that the phase noise is not a fundamental quantity but it is a derived one, and that the phase reduction process is an approximation of the oscillator dynamics, not an exact one.

(i) the phase noise in autonomous oscillators can be decomposed in phase and amplitude noise; (ii) the phase noise is the projection of the oscillator fluctuations onto the phase subspace, which is spanned by the Floquet modes with the same frequency as the unperturbed oscillator; (iii) the orbital fluctuations can be neglected when their amplitude is small, but not necessarily when the phase noise is small.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new theoretical framework to study the noise properties of oscillators, which allows to decompose their fluctuations in terms of amplitude and phase noise.
the study of the noise properties in autonomous oscillators.
the study of the dynamics of oscillators and the effects of noise in them.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, while it is true that a phase reduction is possible for many oscillators, the phase dynamics is not always well defined, and it is always affected by amplitude-related effects, that are often overlooked in the literature.

the noise properties of an autonomous system can only be assessed by a proper decomposition in terms of phase, orbital and amplitude noise and that the phase reduction approach should be applied only when the orbital noise can be neglected.

the phase reduction process is a valid and powerful approach for the study of the noise properties in autonomous oscillators, provided that one keeps in mind the possible limitations and caveats that we point out in the paper.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
phase noise is the noise in the phase of a system that is not in a limit cycle but in a periodic orbit.
phase noise in autonomous oscillators is a very complex phenomenon, whose understanding is still in its infancy.
the phase reduction is an approximate procedure, whose validity is limited by the amplitude fluctuations, that can be assessed by a careful analysis of the reduced system.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the phase reduction process, which is the most commonly used approach for assessing the noise properties of oscillators, is not always possible, and that in the cases where it is possible, the reduced phase model may not always describe the noise properties of the oscillator in a faithful manner.

a rigorous assessment of the phase properties of a noisy oscillator requires the definition of a suitable projection operator that allows to decomposed the system fluctuations in terms of the phase and amplitude fluctuations.
the phase reduction is a very delicate operation, that requires a careful analysis and a careful choice of the projection base.
